> Louhos - Community-driven Source Code for Open Data in Finland
>
> With open data on decision-making, governance, economics and other
> aspects of society rapidly increasing, there is a clear need for free
> and open tools for the exploration and utilization of the new
> information resources. In particular, unified analyses environments
> are needed that would allow seamless integration of various analytical
> tools across different application domains and open data streams from
> heterogeneous sources. The current solutions are limited to specific
> applications, such as geographical information, economical analyses
> and visualization, forming a bottleneck for modularity and
> reproducibility of the analyses. Another essential element for
> realizing the full potential of the new governmental data resources is
> customization to the local needs within each country or region.
> Louhos (louhos.github.com <http://louhos.github.com>) is a
> community-driven project that aims to
> collect a comprehensive code base of source code and tools for open
> data in Finland and to make the analytical tools available through a
> single, organized entry point. The project hosts a comprehensive R
> library soRvi ('turning machine'), which provides programmatic access
> to hundreds of Finnish data resources, and seamless integration to
> professional data analysis and visualization tools. In addition to
> providing data download and preprocessing routines, we develop and
> collect analytical tools, and use these tools for new insights into
> how the society works, through regular blog posts including
> reproducible analyses on local political issues with documented source
> code in local language. The project aims to promote government
> transparency and received a double award in Private Data opening
> category in the national Apps4Finland 2011 competition. We call the
> open data community to launch a network of similar initiatives across
> the globe, suited for local standards and needs and to share the
> efforts, code and fun!
>

messages.body_plain:
Moi, Share-tyypit kaipaa otsikkoa ja lyhytt? abstraktia. Ajattelin
seuraavaa, onko ok tai tuleeko mieleen parannettavaa (otsikkoa varsinkin
mietin viel?)?
/ Leo


Open Tools for Open Data in Finland

A variety of public and private organizations
<http://www.maanmittauslaitos.fi/en/node/6567><http://www.stat.fi/tup/tilastotietokannat/index_en.html>are
now taking steps toward a wider access to data in many countries across the
globe. Automated tools and customization to local standards are essential
for realizing the full potential of the new information resources. The
comprehensive R library for Open Data, coined
*soRvi*<http://louhos.github.com/sorvi/index.html>('turning machine'),
provides programmatic access to hundreds of data
resources in Finland and enables seamless integration of open data streams
with professional data analysis and visualization tools. The toolkit
received a double award in Private Data opening category in the national
Apps4Finland 2011 competition. soRvi is a community-driven project all the
way - we develop and apply analytical tools for new insights into how the
society works. While our focus is on Finnish open data and tools, we call
the open data community to launch a network of similar initiatives, suited
for local standards and needs and to share the efforts, code and fun!

Hello everyone,

The OKFestival core planning team had a meeting this week on Tue & Wed,
here is a photo of us at the OKFestival HACK space (Lume Film Studio):
http://www.flickr.com/photos/okfn/6965889082/in/photostream

Below you can find a summary of the main decisions we made during these
two days. The definitions of the themes (point ONE below) might still
need some fine-tuning, feedback is very welcome! (to planning team
address info at okfestival.org or to this list).

Point THREE below is important - we are looking for more Guest Programme
Planners to join the OKFestival programme planning process. The topic
streamsthat need help are:
? ?- Data Driven Journalism
? ?- Gender / Diversity in Openness
? ?- Open urban/municipal data (transport, public works etc)
? ?- Open national/international government data
? ?- Open economics
? ?- Open business & corporate data

We have a week or so time to bring in new people: we have to fix the
topic streams before we send out the second Call for Proposals on
*Monday 7th of May* (with 1st of June as a deadline).

Best regards,

Juha.

- - - - - - -

OKFESTIVAL 2012 THEMES, TOPIC STREAMS & VENUE SPACES NOW CONFIRMED.

The Core Organising Team has been hard at work this week going through
submissions and topics. We are proud to announce that we have important
updates for preview, and you're the first to hear about them!

# ONE >>> We have confirmed the following 10 guiding THEMES for
OKFestival 2012.

The guiding THEMES are:
? ?01) Open Cultural Heritage andProduction
02) Open Design, Hardware and Manufacturing
03) Open Government and City Data
04) Gender / Diversity in Openness
05) Open Development and Economics
06) Open Research and Education
07) Open Business and Corporate Data
08) Open Democracy and Citizen Participation
09) Open Source Software
10) Data Visualization and Data Journalism
# TWO >>> Each THEME consists of a set of focused TOPIC STREAMS, which
are specific packages of festival programming designed by our Guest
Programme Plannersfrom around the world.

The confirmed TOPIC STREAMS are:
? ?01) _O__pen __C__ultur__al Heritage & Production_
- Open GLAM: Galleries, Libraries, Archives and Museums
? ?- Creative Commons Film Festival
? ?02) Open Design, Hardware and Manufacturing
? ?- the whole theme is covered
? ?03) Open Government and City Data
? ?- Open Geo information
? ?04) Gender / Diversityin Openness
? ?- incubating theme - no organizer yet
? ?05) Open Development and Economics
? ?- Open Development
? ?06) Open Research and Education
? ?- Open Science
? ?- Open Education
? ?07) Open Business and Corporate Data
? ?- Academic topic stream on Open Data in Business
? ?08) Open Democracy and Citizen Participation
? ?- Open Democracy
? ?09) Open Source Software
? ?- Open Source Software organized by http://www.openmind.ficonference
? ?10) Data Visualization and Data Journalism
? ?- Satellite event: Tieto n?kyv?ksi / Making Data Visible(organised
by Aalto University Graphic Design programme)

# THREE >>> WANTED: NEW COLLABORATORS. We are currently looking for
additional participation in the following topics. Each of these topics
have generated a great deal of interest from international communities,
but do not haveenoughGuest Programme Planners yet. As a result, they may
be moved to the unconference sessionof the festival.

The topic streamsthat need help are:
? ?- Data Driven Journalism
? ?- Gender / Diversity in Openness
? ?- Open urban/municipal data (transport, public works etc)
? ?- Open national/international government data
? ?- Open economics
? ?- Open business & corporate data

# FOUR >>> The Core Organising Team is also happy to announce the
following spaces at our 2012 venue, each with a specific theme:

? ?- HACK: Lume Film studio - 4 simultaneous workshops/sessions for max
30-40 persons each
? ?- MAKE: Aalto Media Factory (Auditorium for 50 people + Fablab (for
max 20 people) + 2 meeting rooms (for approx 10 people each))
? ?- INSPIRE: Sampo hall + Foyer (lecture room for 300 people + a large
